papers.title: The Moral Machine Experiment
papers.authors: Awad, E., Dsouza, S., Shariff, A., Rahwan, I., & Bonnefon, J.-F.
papers.abstract_snippet: Massive cross-cultural study of moral preferences in autonomous vehicle dilemmas with 40 million decisions from 233 countries, revealing three moral clusters and strong cultural variation in moral preferences.

papers.title: Situational factors shape moral judgments in the trolley dilemma in Eastern, Western, and Southern countries in a culturally diverse sample
papers.abstract_snippet: Large-scale cross-cultural study showing that situational factors (number of lives, intentionality) shape trolley dilemma moral judgments differently across Eastern, Western, and Southern cultural clusters.

papers.title: The Weirdest People in the World?
papers.authors: Henrich, J., Heine, S. J., & Norenzayan, A.
papers.abstract_snippet: Argues that Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic (WEIRD) populations are outliers on many psychological measures including moral reasoning, questioning the generalizability of psychology research.

papers.title: Universals and variations in moral decisions made in 42 countries by 70,000 participants
papers.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract_snippet: Follow-up to Moral Machine experiment analyzing moral decisions across 42 countries with 70,000 participants, identifying universal moral preferences and systematic cross-cultural variations.

papers.title: Mapping the Moral Domain
papers.authors: Graham, J., Nosek, B. A., Haidt, J., Iyer, R., Koleva, S., & Ditto, P. H.
papers.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
papers.abstract_snippet: Created and validated the Moral Foundations Questionnaire (MFQ) establishing human baseline norms for moral foundations across political orientations and demographics.

papers.title: Morality Beyond the WEIRD: How the Nomological Network of Morality Varies Across Cultures
papers.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
papers.abstract_snippet: Cross-cultural validation of MFT beyond WEIRD populations, showing that the moral domain's structure varies across cultures and that Western-derived moral foundations do not fully capture moral concerns in non-Western societies.

papers.title: An Overview of the Schwartz Theory of Basic Values
papers.venue: Online Readings in Psychology and Culture
papers.abstract_snippet: Comprehensive overview of the Schwartz value theory identifying 10 basic human values organized in a circular motivational continuum, validated across 82 countries. Provides foundational human baselines for value measurement.

papers.title: DIT-2: Devising and Testing a Revised Instrument of Moral Judgment
papers.authors: Rest, J. R., Narvaez, D., Thoma, S. J., & Bebeau, M. J.
papers.abstract_snippet: Presents the revised Defining Issues Test (DIT-2) for measuring moral judgment development based on Kohlberg's stages, with extensive norming data providing human baselines across age groups and education levels.

papers.title: Large language models show amplified cognitive biases in moral decision-making
papers.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract_snippet: Compares LLM moral decision-making to human baselines, showing that models exhibit amplified versions of known cognitive biases, with systematic deviations from human norms.

papers.title: Assessing the Alignment of Large Language Models with Human Values Using the Portrait Values Questionnaire
papers.abstract_snippet: Compares LLM value profiles to human baselines from 53,000 human respondents using the PVQ-RR, finding systematic differences in how models express values compared to diverse human populations.
